Conceived in the 1970s, high-energy dual-axis radiography was fully realized in 2010 with the completion of A2. As the accelerators approach mid-design life (when compared to PHERMEX or other large accelerator facilities), opportunities to en- hance and strengthen both infrastructure and major systems issues have been identified. Successful implementa- tion of the actions presented in this strategy will mitigate issues and leverage opportunities, ensuring continuation of high operational readiness and augmenting performance across many facets for the mission activities. These two areas will be addressed separately and supported with ancillary background. DARHT Facility, Maintenance, and Infrastructure The DARHT Facility is nearing 25 years of continuous operation. Other facilities within the DARHT Complex have exceeded 50 years of continuous use. There is a growing list of repairs, updates, and modernization efforts needed across the 12 total existing facilities to sustain this one-of-a-kind capability for the nation. To keep the DARHT Com- plex facilities operating reliably for the next 20-plus years, a comprehensive suite of advancements must be made to ensure reliable and resilient operations. On an individual basis, these projects are being planned during scheduled maintenance windows to allow an appropriate balance of experimental work and maintenance to be performed on an annual basis.
